channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Consolidation risk after recent gains against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong expect USD/SGD to consolidate as earlier Singapore Dollar (SGD) gains face a modest US Dollar (USD) rebound and position unwinding ahead of United States (US) core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index data and Jackson Hole.

item.title: Australia CPI expected to show inflation easing in July
item.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) will publish the July Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Wednesday at 01:30 GMT. The report is expected to show that inflation rose 3.2% from a year earlier, easing from the 3.8% posted in June.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls hold 217.00 after trendline break
item.description: The GBP/JPY surpassed a downtrend resistance line and reclaimed the 217.00 level on Tuesday, as the Japanese Yen weakened while Sterling pushed to a new three-week high at 217.48. At the time of writing, the cross-pair trades at 217.31, up 0.20%.

item.title: Mexican Peso holds below 16.95 as traders eye US data, Iran shift
item.description: The Mexican Peso holds firm near 10-year highs against the US Dollar on Tuesday, as the USD/MXN pair sits below the 16.95 level while investors digest US economic data and recent developments between the US and Iran. The exotic pair trades at 16.94, virtually unchanged.

item.title: Thai Baht: Bullish bias against US Dollar faces BoT sensitivity – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that Thai Baht (THB) has rallied to a two‑month high on softer US Dollar (USD), lower Oil prices, strong electronics exports and Gold-related flows.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Bullish bias with focus on 6.7000 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann maintain a negative stance on USD/CNH, noting a softened underlying tone even as recent price action stayed relatively quiet. Intraday, they see scope for a modest drift lower while keeping 6.7150 as key support.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar climbs to fresh highs amid timid US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD climbed to around 0.5980 Tuesday, near its highest level since June 1 as a softer US Dollar (USD) and firm Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) rate-hike expectations powered the Kiwi higher.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range-bound consolidation outlook against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao note that USD/SGD has eased from 1.2800 to around 1.2700 as the softer US Dollar (USD) and global risk sentiment dominate.

item.title: US-Iran agree ceasefire deal, sinks Oil – RIA Novosti
item.description: The Russian agency RIA Novosti reported on Tuesday that Washington and Tehran agreed to a ceasefire, citing sources in Iran and Pakistan.

item.title: US Treasury yields fall as Hormuz progress eases inflation fears
item.description: US yields edge lower across the whole curve on Tuesday, following suit.

item.title: South Korean Won: Strength backed by tech flows against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts highlight that the Korean Won (KRW) has gained 12% versus the Dollar year-to-date, with USD/KRW falling from around 1560 in June to below 1380.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Trade risks limit gains against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that reports of potential US tariffs on Chinese goods and the PBoC’s resistance to rapid Renminbi (RMB) gains are likely to limit further downside in USD/CNH.

item.title: The US Dollar Index stops paying for hawks who cannot vote
item.description: A non-voting regional Federal Reserve president published a conditional hold on Tuesday, tying the current target range to continued evidence that inflation is actually coming down, and the Dollar Index has not moved for it.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar stays on the back foot ahead of PCE
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) is hovering below the 99.00 mark as traders squared positions ahead of a heavy Wednesday data slate and Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address on Friday.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside momentum eases against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD remains under mild downward pressure but short-term momentum is flat, keeping the pair in a tight intraday band around 1.2700.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD reclaims 100-day SMA, eyes $70
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price registers modest gains on Tuesday, after briefly breaching the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at $68.38, pushing the white metal to a three-day low of $67.43 before making a U-turn and turning bullish. The XAG/USD pair trades at $68.86, up 0.55%,

item.title: Gold pulls back from $4,700 as Hormuz hopes cool haven demand
item.description: Gold price holds firm during the North American session as buyers fail to surpass the $4,700 level, exacerbating a retracement below a key psychological level, amid mixed US data and rising hopes for an end to the US-Iran conflict. XAU/USD traded at $4,641, down 0.2%.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Bearish indicators keep the path tilted lower
item.description: USD/CAD edges lower on Tuesday, with the Canadian Dollar (CAD) drawing support from a weaker US Dollar (USD) as traders also assess the latest tit-for-tat tariff measures between the United States (US) and Canada.

item.title: Euro remains flat with Sterling despite upbeat German data
item.description: EUR/GBP traded around 0.8560 on Tuesday, little changed, as a run of stronger German data failed to give the Euro (EUR) a clear lift against a resilient Pound. The pair remains pinned near its 20 and 100-period Simple Moving Averages (SMA), with neither side able to force a break.

item.title: Japanese Yen remains vulnerable despite softer Greenback
item.description: USD/JPY extends its sideways movement below the 160.00 mark on Tuesday, holding modest gains despite a softer US Dollar (USD). The weaker Greenback has failed to lift the Japanese Yen (JPY), which is underperforming its major peers. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 159.30.

item.title: Germany: Political risks cloud reform outlook – ING
item.description: ING’s Carsten Brzeski highlights how upcoming state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin could reshape German politics and indirectly affect the economy.

item.title: Mexico: Alignment for certainty in USMCA – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Dev Ashish argues that Mexico could benefit from tensions between the US and Canada, but warns that uncertainty around USMCA may limit the upside.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average round-trips between Ottawa and the Treasury
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average has built a 300-point advance and handed every point of it back inside a single vertical break, and it trades just beneath 53,500 for a gain of roughly a tenth of a percent. The session range runs better than 320 points against a net of 67.

item.title: United Kingdom: Resilient growth versus fiscal strain – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley highlights that recent UK data, including Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP), real output per head and the August composite Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), point to resilient growth and improved consumer confidence.

item.title: Canadian Dollar faces double trouble from Oil slump, US tariffs
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3835 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down a modest 0.07% on the day. The pair lacks a clear direction as both the US Dollar (USD) and the Canadian Dollar (CAD) face headwinds.

item.title: Germany: Business climate brightens – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Ralph Solveen notes that the German Ifo Business Climate Index rose from 86.7 to 88.8 in August, with both current conditions and expectations improving. He highlights stronger foreign demand, rising government spending and better sentiment as factors supporting growth.

item.title: British Pound holds near six-month high as Hormuz hopes lift sentiment
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) consolidates near a six-month high of 1.3675 on Tuesday as Middle East headlines improve risk appetite, while investors await the release of key US economic data and the speech by Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole.

item.title: Eurozone: AfD surge raises policy uncertainty – ING
item.description: Carsten Brzeski of ING underscores that the AfD’s rise to Germany’s largest party in polls introduces significant uncertainty for Eurozone policy.

item.title: Australian Dollar up modestly on RBA, weak USD
item.description: AUD/USD steadies around the mid 0.7100s at the time of writing on Tuesday, clawing back most of the previous day's modest losses.

item.title: British Pound: Range-bound against US Dollar ahead of Budget – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight GBP/USD consolidating in a tight mid-1.36 range as a quiet data and Bank of England (BoE) calendar contrasts with softer yield spreads, which have eroded some fundamental support.
